title: Brake System Inspection
intro: Inspection is the foundation of brake maintenance. A careful, logical inspection finds wear and faults before they become failures, and it tells you which parts actually need attention. This chapter gives a structured method for fifteen inspection items.
objectives: Follow a consistent seven-point method for each inspection.
Recognise normal and defective conditions of brake components.
Link a defect to likely causes.
Decide on a safe next action.

blocks: Each inspection card answers seven questions: **what** to inspect, **why** it matters, **how** to inspect, what **normal** looks like, what **defective** looks like, possible **causes**, and the **recommended next action**.

blocks.warn: Limits such as minimum pad thickness, rotor thickness, runout and drum diameter are different for every vehicle. This guide never gives them. Always compare your measurements with the manufacturer's service manual.

blocks.tip: Inspect in a consistent order, and record findings as you go. Compare left with right on the same axle: a difference is often more revealing than a single reading.

insp.title: 1. Brake pedal condition and operation
insp.what: Pedal height, free play, firmness, return, and pedal pad and linkage.
insp.why: The pedal is the driver's connection to the whole system. Its feel reveals air, leaks, booster faults and sticking.
how: With the engine off, press the pedal several times and note the feel.
Press and hold with moderate force for about 30 seconds; it should not sink.
Start the engine while holding the pedal; it should move slightly down.
Check the pedal returns fully and moves smoothly, and the pad is in good condition.
insp.normal: Firm pedal that holds steady, returns fully, and has the travel and height given by the manufacturer.
insp.defective: Soft, spongy, hard, low, or sinking pedal; sticking; unusual noises; excessive free play.
insp.causes: Air or moisture in the fluid, leaks, worn master cylinder seals, booster fault, brake out of adjustment, worn pedal bushings.
insp.action: Do not drive if the pedal sinks or is very soft. Inspect for leaks, check fluid level, and refer for diagnosis.

insp.title: 2. Brake fluid level
insp.why: A low level means a leak or worn friction parts, and can let air into the system.
how: Park the vehicle on level ground.
Look at the reservoir MIN and MAX marks without opening the cap, if the reservoir is translucent.
Wipe the area before removing the cap, if you must open it.
insp.normal: Fluid between MIN and MAX. A small drop over time is normal as pads wear.
insp.defective: Level below MIN, rapid drop, or a level that is higher than MAX after parts were changed.
insp.causes: Leak, worn pads, fluid loss during service, or overfilling.
insp.action: Do not simply top up and ignore it. Find out why the level is low. Top up only with the specified fluid if the system is otherwise sound.

insp.title: 3. Brake fluid condition
insp.what: Colour, clarity and contamination of the fluid.
insp.why: Old or contaminated fluid lowers the heat resistance of the fluid, and encourages corrosion.
how: Look at the fluid in the reservoir with a good light.
Compare to fresh fluid in a clear container.
Use a fluid test method approved by the manufacturer or workshop, if available.
insp.normal: Clear to light amber (for many fluids), with no particles.
insp.defective: Dark brown or black, cloudy, with particles, or smelling burnt.
insp.causes: Age, moisture absorption, heat, worn seals, or contamination with oil or the wrong fluid.
insp.action: Plan fluid replacement and bleeding. If oil contamination is suspected (rubber seals swelling), refer for a full system inspection.

insp.title: 4. Master cylinder
insp.what: Body, rear seal area, line connections and reservoir.
insp.why: A failing master cylinder can cause pedal sinking and loss of braking.
how: Look for fluid around the body and at the rear where it meets the booster.
Inspect the reservoir and cap seal.
Check the lines at the cylinder for dampness.
Hold the pedal and watch for sinking.
insp.normal: Dry, clean, tight connections; steady pedal.
insp.defective: Wet areas, fluid in the booster or on the firewall, cracked reservoir, sinking pedal.
insp.causes: Worn internal seals, corrosion, loose fittings, old fluid.
insp.action: Replace or repair under supervision following the manufacturer's procedure, then bleed the system.

insp.title: 5. Brake lines
insp.what: Rigid steel lines and their fittings from the master cylinder to the hoses.
insp.why: A damaged line can leak or burst under pressure.
how: Look along the full run, including clips and fittings, using a light.
Look for damp or wet spots, rust, dents, kinks, rubbing.
Check clips and brackets are secure.
insp.normal: Dry, straight, clean lines with secure clips and no heavy rust.
insp.defective: Leaks, corrosion pits, flaking rust, kinks, rubbing wear.
insp.causes: Age, road salt and moisture, impacts, poor routing after repairs.
insp.action: Do not drive with a leaking line. Replace the damaged section using correct brake tubing and fittings, then bleed.

insp.title: 6. Brake hoses
insp.why: Hoses age and flex, and failure causes loss of braking at the wheel or pressure trapped in a brake.
how: Inspect the full length of each hose with a light.
Look for cracks, swelling, chafing, leaks at the ends.
Check hoses with the steering turned to each side if possible, that they do not rub.
Check the hose is not twisted.
insp.normal: Smooth, dry, flexible hose with no cracks, bulges or rubbing.
insp.defective: Cracks, bulges, wet fittings, chafed outer covering, twisted or stiff hose.
insp.causes: Ageing, heat, rubbing, incorrect installation, internal collapse.
insp.action: Replace defective hoses in pairs on an axle as the manufacturer recommends, and bleed the system.

insp.title: 7. Brake calipers
insp.what: Caliper body, piston, boot, slide pins, brackets and bleeder screws.
insp.why: A seized or leaking caliper reduces braking, causes pulling, or overheating.
how: Look for fluid leaks around the piston, boot and hose connection.
Check the dust boot for tears.
Check slide pins move freely and boots are intact.
After a drive, carefully compare hub or wheel temperatures left and right, using caution as parts can be hot.
insp.normal: Dry, clean caliper with a sound boot, sliding freely.
insp.defective: Fluid at the piston, torn boot, rust on the piston, stuck slide pins, one wheel hotter than the other.
insp.causes: Water and dirt entering through a damaged boot, lack of lubrication, old fluid, age.
insp.action: Service or replace the caliper under supervision, replace pads as a set on the axle, and bleed.

insp.title: 8. Brake pads
insp.what: Friction material thickness, wear pattern and condition.
insp.why: Pads are the main wear item. Worn-out pads damage rotors and reduce braking.
how: Look at the pads through the caliper or remove the wheel to see both inner and outer pads.
Measure the remaining friction material and compare it to the manufacturer's minimum.
Compare inner and outer pad, and left and right.
Check for cracks, glazing, contamination and a loose pad.
insp.normal: Even wear, friction material above the minimum, clean and dry, no cracks.
insp.defective: Thin material, uneven or tapered wear, glazed surface, oil or fluid contamination, cracks, pad coming apart.
insp.causes: Normal wear, sticking caliper or slide pins, incorrect pads, hard driving, contamination.
insp.action: Replace pads in axle sets when at or near the limit. Find the cause of uneven wear before fitting new pads.

insp.title: 9. Brake discs (rotors)
insp.what: Surface condition, thickness, runout and edge lip.
insp.why: A damaged disc reduces braking and causes vibration.
how: Look at both faces of the disc for scoring, cracks, rust and heat marks.
Feel the edge for a ridge (lip).
Measure thickness in several places with a micrometer and compare to the minimum marked on the disc or in the manual.
Measure runout with a dial indicator, comparing to the manufacturer's limit.
insp.normal: Smooth, even surface with light polish from the pads; thickness above the minimum; runout within the limit.
insp.defective: Deep grooves, cracks, blue discolouration, heavy rust ridge, thickness below minimum, excessive runout, pulsing in the pedal.
insp.causes: Worn pads, overheating, uneven tightening of wheel nuts, a stuck caliper, corrosion from lack of use.
insp.action: Resurface only if the thickness will remain above the minimum. Otherwise replace discs in axle pairs.

insp.title: 10. Brake drums
insp.what: Inner surface condition, diameter and roundness.
insp.why: A scored or oversized drum cannot brake properly or safely.
how: Remove the drum following the manual (the adjuster may need to be backed off).
Look for scoring, cracks, hard spots, rust and contamination.
Measure the inside diameter in several places and compare to the maximum diameter marked on the drum or in the manual.
Check for a lip at the edge of the friction surface.
insp.normal: Smooth, even surface with diameter within the limit and no cracks.
insp.defective: Deep scoring, cracks, blue spots, out-of-round, diameter beyond the limit.
insp.causes: Worn linings, contamination, overheating, wrong adjustment.
insp.action: Machine only within the limit. Replace if beyond the limit or cracked.

insp.title: 11. Brake shoes
insp.what: Lining thickness, condition, springs and hold-down hardware.
insp.why: Worn or contaminated shoes reduce braking and the parking brake action.
how: Inspect the lining thickness against the manufacturer's minimum.
Check for oil, grease or fluid contamination.
Check the lining is secure and not cracked.
Check springs, clips and hold-downs for damage.
insp.normal: Dry linings with even wear above the minimum thickness; springs in good condition.
insp.defective: Thin or cracked linings, glazing, contamination, weak or broken springs.
insp.causes: Wear, leaking wheel cylinder or axle seal, over-adjustment, age.
insp.action: Replace shoes in axle sets. Find and repair the source of any contamination.

insp.title: 12. Wheel cylinders
insp.why: Leaks contaminate the linings and reduce braking.
how: Carefully lift the dust boots to look for fluid.
Look for dampness on the backing plate and shoes.
Check for seized pistons by observing shoe movement when someone presses the pedal (under supervision).
insp.defective: Fluid inside the boot, wet shoes, torn boot, seized piston.
insp.causes: Worn seals, old fluid, corrosion, age.
insp.action: Replace or rebuild the cylinder per manual, replace contaminated shoes, bleed.

insp.title: 13. Parking brake
insp.what: Lever or pedal travel, cable condition, holding ability, and release.
insp.why: The parking brake holds the vehicle when parked and can be an emergency back-up.
how: Count the number of lever clicks or the pedal travel and compare to the manual.
Check the cables and boots for rust, fraying or sticking.
Check the wheels turn freely when released.
Test holding on a safe, gentle slope, ready to use the service brake.
insp.normal: Applies and releases smoothly with the travel specified.
insp.defective: Excessive travel, sticking, will not hold, will not release, noises.
insp.causes: Stretched or seized cables, worn rear linings, mis-adjustment, seized levers.
insp.action: Adjust or replace per the manufacturer. Electric parking brakes need the proper service mode and procedure.

insp.title: 14. Brake warning lights
insp.what: The red brake warning light and related indicators.
insp.why: They give early notice of low fluid, parking brake status and hydraulic faults.
how: Turn the ignition on without starting; the light should illuminate (bulb check).
Start the engine; the light should go out.
Apply and release the parking brake and watch the light.
If the light stays on with the parking brake released, check fluid level.
insp.normal: Light comes on during bulb check, goes out after starting, and responds to the parking brake.
insp.defective: Light stays on, flashes, or never lights.
insp.causes: Low fluid, parking brake switch, hydraulic imbalance, a failed bulb or wiring.
insp.action: If the red light stays on while driving, stop safely and do not continue until inspected.

insp.title: 15. ABS warning lights
insp.why: It shows whether ABS is working. When off, ABS is unavailable but normal braking remains in most vehicles.
how: Turn the ignition on; the light should come on briefly and go out.
If it stays on, read the fault codes with an appropriate scan tool.
Check wheel speed sensor wiring, sensor condition and tone ring for damage or debris.
insp.normal: Light comes on during the check and goes out within seconds.
insp.defective: Light stays on, comes on while driving, or flashes.
insp.causes: Wheel speed sensor faults, damaged tone rings, wiring faults, low voltage, hydraulic unit faults.
insp.action: Diagnose using the scan tool and service manual. Drive with caution until repaired.

concepts: Use the same seven questions for every inspection.
Compare left and right sides of an axle.
Never rely on appearance alone: measure and compare with specifications.
A leak is always a defect, however small.
examples: Inner pad is much thinner than the outer pad. The caliper slide pins are likely sticking, so cleaning and lubricating them (or replacing the caliper) should accompany the new pads.
The pedal slowly sinks when held. The master cylinder, a leaking line, or a leaking wheel cylinder are possible causes. The vehicle must not be driven until the cause is found.
A rear drum has fluid inside. A wheel cylinder leak is likely, and the shoes must be replaced.
safety: Never use your mouth or hands to check for fluid under pressure; use a light and a clean rag.
Hot brake parts can burn. Allow parts to cool before touching.
Pedal tests with the vehicle on stands must be done only with the wheels secured and under supervision.
practice: Take any brake photograph or real component and answer the seven questions for it.
Compare left and right pad wear on a vehicle, if available, and write down any difference.

check.q: Why is it useful to compare left and right sides?
check.a: A difference between sides can reveal a fault such as a sticking caliper, even if each reading alone seems acceptable.

check.q: What should you do if the brake fluid level is low?
check.a: Find out why. Do not just top up and ignore a leak or worn pads.

check.q: What does uneven inner and outer pad wear often indicate?
check.a: Sticking caliper slide pins or piston.

check.q: How do you know the minimum rotor thickness?
check.a: From the marking on the rotor or the manufacturer's service manual.

check.q: What should you do if the red brake light stays on when driving?
check.a: Stop safely and arrange for inspection before driving further.

summary: Inspect in a repeatable order using the seven-point method.
Measure and compare with the manufacturer's limits.
Treat any leak, soft pedal or warning light as a safety issue.
